resumen: La pasiva se forma con be en el tiempo que corresponda + participio: These laptops are made in Taiwan. Our school was built in 1965.
En los tiempos continuos se añade being y en los perfectos been: The room is being cleaned. Our table had already been given to another couple.
Con modales: modal + be + participio (Phones must be switched off) y, para el pasado, modal + have been + participio (The accident could have been avoided).
Infinitivo pasivo to be + participio y gerundio pasivo being + participio: All applications have to be submitted online. Nobody likes being criticised.

Con verbos de dos objetos (give, offer, send, show) lo normal es que la persona sea el sujeto: My sister has been offered a scholarship. Explain no lo admite: It was explained to us, no We were explained.
Pasiva impersonal con say, think, believe, expect: It is said that he is rich o He is said to be rich; para un hecho anterior, to have + participio: They are thought to have left.
by introduce a quien hace la acción y with el instrumento: painted by a famous artist with a fine brush. Si el agente no importa o es obvio, se omite.
make en pasiva recupera el to: They made us wait → We were made to wait.

preguntas.x: La pasiva en presente se forma con am/is/are + participio: are made. These laptops make diría que los portátiles fabrican algo, y are make usa el infinitivo en lugar del participio.
Para un hecho terminado con fecha (in 1965) se usa past simple pasivo: was built. Has been built no combina con una fecha pasada, y Our school built diría que la escuela construyó algo.

preguntas.q: Mobile phones must ___ off during the exam.
preguntas.x: Tras un modal, la pasiva se forma con be + participio: must be switched off. Must switched omite be, y must been no existe porque después del modal va el infinitivo.

preguntas.q: The winners ___ by email next week.
preguntas.x: La pasiva en futuro es will be + participio: will be informed. Will inform y will be informing son activas y dirían que los ganadores van a informar a alguien.

preguntas.q: The portrait was painted ___ a famous artist ___ a very fine brush.
preguntas.x: En la pasiva, by introduce a quien hace la acción (by a famous artist) y with el instrumento que usa (with a brush). From no introduce al agente: es un error que viene de «un cuadro de...».

preguntas.q: Sorry, you can't use this room — it ___ at the moment.
preguntas.x: Para una acción pasiva en curso se usa is being + participio: it's being cleaned. It is cleaning diría que la sala limpia algo, e is cleaned describe un hábito, no algo que ocurre at the moment.

preguntas.q: When we arrived at the restaurant, our table ___ to another couple, so we had to wait at the bar.
preguntas.x: Para algo que otros hicieron antes de un momento pasado se usa past perfect pasivo: had already been given. Had already given es activa (la mesa habría dado algo), y has been given no encaja en un relato en pasado.

preguntas.q: Nobody likes ___ by their boss in front of their colleagues.
preguntas.x: By their boss exige una forma pasiva, y tras like la pasiva va en gerundio (being criticised) o en infinitivo con to (to be criticised). Criticising y to criticise son activas, y be criticised sin to no puede seguir a like.

preguntas.q: All applications have ___ online by 31 May.
preguntas.x: Tras have to, la pasiva se forma con to be + participio: have to be submitted. Have to submit es activa (las solicitudes no envían nada) y to be submitting es continua, no pasiva.

preguntas.q: It ___ that the new metro line will open next year.
preguntas.x: La pasiva impersonal It is expected that... presenta una opinión general sin decir quién la tiene. It expects o it is expecting harían de it el sujeto que espera algo, lo cual no tiene sentido.

preguntas.a: The new procedure was explained to us by the manager.
d: We were explained the new procedure by the manager.
The new procedure was explained us by the manager.
To us was explained the new procedure by the manager.
preguntas.x: Explain no admite dos objetos, así que la persona no puede ser el sujeto de la pasiva: It was explained to us. We were explained calca «nos explicaron», y sin to la frase tampoco funciona.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “They have offered my sister a scholarship.”
preguntas.a: My sister has been offered a scholarship.
d: My sister has offered a scholarship.
A scholarship has been offered my sister.
My sister has been offering a scholarship.
preguntas.x: Con verbos de dos objetos como offer, lo más natural es que la persona sea el sujeto de la pasiva: My sister has been offered a scholarship. My sister has offered es activa y cambia el sentido, y si el sujeto es la cosa hace falta to (offered to my sister).

preguntas.q: That email should ___ to the whole team yesterday, not just to me.
preguntas.x: Para criticar algo que no se hizo en el pasado, en pasiva, se usa should have been + participio. Should be sent se refiere al presente o al futuro y choca con yesterday, y should have sent es activa (el correo no envía nada).

preguntas.q: The thieves are thought ___ the country last night.
preguntas.x: En la pasiva personal (They are thought...), un hecho anterior se expresa con infinitivo perfecto: to have left. To leave no encaja con last night, y that solo va con la construcción impersonal (It is thought that they left).

preguntas.q: The accident ___ if the driver had been paying attention.
preguntas.x: Para una posibilidad pasada que no se cumplió, en pasiva, se usa could have been + participio. The accident could have avoided es activa (el accidente no evita nada), y could be avoided no se refiere al pasado.

preguntas.q: We were made ___ for two hours before anyone attended to us.
preguntas.x: En activa make va con infinitivo sin to (They made us wait), pero en pasiva el to reaparece: We were made to wait. We were made wait es el error más común.

preguntas.a: It is believed that the painting was stolen in the 1990s.
d: It is believed the painting to have been stolen in the 1990s.
The painting is believed that it was stolen in the 1990s.
The painting is believed to be stolen in the 1990s.
preguntas.x: Hay dos formas correctas: It is believed that + oración, o The painting is believed to have been stolen. No se mezclan, y para un hecho pasado el infinitivo debe ser perfecto (to have been stolen), no to be stolen.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “People say that the new manager is very demanding.”
preguntas.a: The new manager is said to be very demanding.
d: The new manager is said that he is very demanding.
The new manager says to be very demanding.
It is said the new manager to be very demanding.
preguntas.x: People say that X... puede pasar a X is said to + infinitivo o a It is said that.... No se mezcla X is said con that, y The new manager says cambiaría el sentido: sería él quien lo dice.
